question: Where should a tourniquet be placed on an injured limb?

question: What type of tissue makes up the outer layer of the skin, the epidermis?

question: Which task best describes a nurse acting as an environmental manager in the ward?

question: Why is knowing how a poison entered the body important in emergency care?

question: What is the most appropriate action after removing gloves used during stool collection?

options.A: Wipe hands with a dry paper towel

options.A: Glucose

question: What is the main waste gas that the respiratory system removes from the body?

options.A: Nitrogen gas

question: What kind of event can trigger a sudden thyroid storm in a patient who has hyperthyroidism?

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended way for a midwife to handle pre-operative anxiety?

question: How long is exclusive breastfeeding recommended before introducing complementary foods?

question: What book is used to keep a continuous written record of dangerous drugs in the ward?

question: What is the main tissue type found in the tunica media of muscular arteries?

options.A: Simple squamous epithelium

question: What timeframe is known as the golden hour during critical obstetric complications?

options.A: The sixty minutes spent completing ward shift handovers

question: Why should healthcare workers care about a patient's emotions just as much as their physical cuts and bruises?

options.A: Physical injuries never cause any psychological changes

question: A midwife is asked to help move a heavy patient alone because the mechanical lift is in another ward. What is the safest course of action?

question: Why is crossing over during meiosis important?

question: A student finishes practicing a perineal suture repair but misses a key aseptic step. How should the lecturer provide feedback?

question: How does involving a supportive family member during pre-operative preparation help the expectant mother?

question: A midwife is collecting blood for cross-matching from a restless patient. What is the most important safety step?

options.B: Ask a relative to confirm the patient's name from outside the ward
options.C: Label the tube at the nurse's station to save time during an emergency
options.D: Wait until the doctor arrives to draw the sample personally

explanation: Labelling tubes away from the patient is a major cause of fatal clerical errors; bedside verification and labelling are mandatory. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T8#BMP111_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of putting a urinary catheter in an unconscious patient?

options.A: To stop the need for daily washing
options.B: To give liquid medicines through the tube
options.C: To prevent the belly from swelling up
options.D: To measure urine output accurately and keep skin dry

explanation: A catheter makes it easy to track fluid balance and protects delicate skin from moisture damage. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T1#BMP120_U5_T1_h5)

question: Which degree of perineal tear involves the anal sphincter muscles but not the rectal mucosa?

options.A: Third-degree tear
options.B: First-degree tear
options.C: Second-degree tear
options.D: Fourth-degree tear

explanation: A third-degree tear involves injury to the perineal muscles and the anal sphincter complex, while fourth-degree tears also tear through the rectal lining. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T7#BMP210_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which physical movement helps push blood up the leg veins during walking?

options.A: Arterial pulse pressure wave
options.B: Atrial contraction rhythm
options.C: Respiratory inhalation cycle
options.D: Skeletal muscle pump

explanation: The skeletal muscle pump uses the contraction of surrounding limb muscles to physically squeeze blood upward through the veins. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T16#BMP111_U5_T16_h3)

question: A patient has a deep wound on the heel where the heel bone is clearly visible. Which stage is this?

options.A: Stage 3
options.B: Unstageable
options.C: Stage 2
options.D: Stage 4

explanation: Exposure of bone, muscle, or tendon classifies a pressure injury as Stage 4 due to deep tissue destruction. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T6#BMP110_U5_T6_h3)

question: A midwife is preparing a mother for discharge. Who should ideally be included in the counseling session to enhance home support?

options.A: No one else to maintain strict privacy
options.B: A partner or trusted family member
options.C: Only the hospital security personnel
options.D: An unfamiliar neighbor waiting outside

explanation: Involving family members helps share the responsibility of post-discharge care and ensures reinforcement of advice at home. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why is mild inflammation a helpful and necessary part of tissue repair?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for collagen production
options.B: It stops all blood circulation so the tissue can rest
options.C: It permanently closes the skin gap within a few minutes
options.D: It brings infection-fighting cells and growth factors to the area

explanation: Inflammation increases blood flow to deliver white blood cells and growth factors essential for clearing debris and starting repair. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h4)

question: You are handing over a hemorrhaging patient to an emergency team. What crucial detail about an applied tourniquet must you share?

options.A: The color of the fabric strap
options.B: The brand name of the device
options.C: The name of the nurse who bought it
options.D: The exact time it was applied

explanation: Receiving clinicians need to know how long the limb has had restricted blood flow to guide surgical decisions. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T3#BMP110_U7_T3_h6)

question: Why is a pudendal nerve block helpful for pain relief during an instrumental vaginal delivery?

options.A: It blocks parasympathetic impulses to the urinary bladder
options.B: It relaxes the smooth muscle fibres inside the uterine body
options.C: It numbs the somatic sensory fibers supplying the lower vagina and perineum
options.D: It stops sympathetic vasoconstriction in the femoral vessels

explanation: Blocking the pudendal nerve desensitizes the perineal tissues, providing excellent pain relief for repairs and instrumental births. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h5)

question: How does the ACTH stimulation test confirm a diagnosis of Addison's disease?

options.A: The adrenal glands fail to produce more cortisol after the injection
options.B: The blood pressure drops dangerously low immediately following the test
options.C: The skin hyperpigmentation disappears within minutes of the injection
options.D: The pituitary gland stops releasing hormones entirely

explanation: Healthy adrenal glands will respond to synthetic ACTH by releasing cortisol, but diseased glands cannot produce an adequate response. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T7#BMP216_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is an essential communication skill for a midwife during antenatal counseling?

options.A: Using technical Latin terms to demonstrate professional authority
options.B: Insisting that the patient follows instructions without asking questions
options.C: Using active listening and clear language free of complex medical jargon
options.D: Speaking rapidly to cover all hospital rules within five minutes

explanation: Clear and empathetic communication ensures that expectant mothers truly understand their health status and birth plans. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T15#BMP212_U1_T15_h7)

question: Why is mixed feeding strongly discouraged for HIV-positive mothers who are breastfeeding?

options.A: It makes the infant's prophylactic syrups completely useless in the body
options.B: It causes the mother's breast milk to dry up prematurely within weeks
options.C: It irritates the baby's immature gut and increases the risk of HIV transmission
options.D: It prevents the infant from receiving routine immunizations at the clinic

explanation: Introducing other liquids or foods damages the delicate intestinal mucosa, making it much easier for the virus in breast milk to enter the infant's bloodstream. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T6#BMP213_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the best action when a midwife finds a clear pelvic contraction during antenatal care?

options.A: Refer the patient for facility delivery with surgical capabilities
options.B: Prescribe muscle relaxants to widen the pelvic bones
options.C: Encourage prolonged active labor exercises at home
options.D: Advise the woman to plan for a home birth with a traditional birth attendant

explanation: A contracted pelvis requires giving birth in a center where a Caesarean section can be safely done if labor gets blocked. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T8#BMP210_U1_T8_h6)

question: What happens to very large medication particles during inhalation?

options.A: They get trapped in the mouth and throat
options.B: They evaporate before reaching the vocal cords
options.C: They pass straight through the alveoli into the blood
options.D: They dissolve instantly in the nasal passages

explanation: Heavy, oversized particles cannot make the sharp turns in the upper airway and deposit in the oropharynx instead. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T5#BMP120_U2_T5_h2)

question: At what gestational age is delivery usually planned for a woman with well-controlled chronic hypertension and no other complications?

options.A: 28 to 30 weeks
options.B: 41 to 42 weeks
options.C: 38 to 39 weeks
options.D: 34 to 35 weeks

explanation: For stable chronic hypertension without complications, delivery is usually scheduled between 38 and 39 weeks to balance fetal maturity against risks. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T3#BMP221_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which clinical situation should a midwife handle FIRST during a busy shift?

options.A: A postpartum client experiencing heavy vaginal bleeding
options.B: An antenatal client asking questions about meal plans
options.C: A laboring mother requesting a warm bath for relaxation
options.D: A postnatal mother waiting for her discharge health talk

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is a life-threatening emergency that ranks highest in clinical priority according to safety frameworks. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T4#BMP120_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard use of passive immunisation?

options.A: Stopping rhesus incompatibility reactions in pregnant women
options.B: Preventing disease after a deep puncture wound contaminated with soil
options.C: Providing immediate antibody cover following a rabid animal bite
options.D: Building lifelong immunity through routine childhood measles vaccination

explanation: Vaccines stimulate active immunity and long-term memory, which is different from passive immunization. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h5)

question: What is one of the most common occupational injuries reported by nurses and midwives?

options.A: Chronic ear infections
options.B: Visual impairment
options.C: Lower back pain
options.D: Fractured collarbones

explanation: Lifting and transferring patients repeatedly without proper body mechanics frequently results in lower back strain and injury. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which specific layer of the dermis lies closest to the epidermis?

options.A: Reticular layer
options.B: Papillary layer
options.C: Subcutaneous layer
options.D: Hypodermis layer

explanation: The papillary layer forms the upper 20 percent of the dermis and touches the basal layer of the epidermis. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T2#BMP111_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the name of the vessel that carries oxygen-rich blood away from the placenta?

options.A: Ductus venosus
options.B: Inferior vena cava
options.C: Umbilical vein
options.D: Umbilical artery

explanation: Unlike adult systemic veins, the umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta straight to the fetal body. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h2)

question: How does the lack of a direct blood supply affect cartilage tissue?

options.A: It relies entirely on active transport proteins on the cell surface to pump in oxygen
options.B: It becomes extremely hard and brittle due to the rapid deposition of calcium phosphate
options.C: It heals very slowly after an injury because nutrients must diffuse from nearby tissues
options.D: It undergoes constant remodeling and daily turnover driven by osteoclast activity

explanation: Cartilage lacks direct blood vessels, which makes metabolic exchange slow and means tissue repair takes a long time. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h4)

question: What practical advice should a midwife give to a rural Nigerian mother who cooks with firewood indoors?

options.A: Improve kitchen ventilation or use cleaner cooking methods
options.B: Stop drinking clean water immediately during meal preparation
options.C: Keep all windows and doors tightly shut while cooking
options.D: Burn wet leaves instead of dry wood to eliminate smoke

explanation: Reducing indoor smoke exposure by improving ventilation protects the respiratory tract from chronic irritation. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T5#BMP125_U1_T5_h8)

question: Why do patients with a pulmonary embolism often have a fast heart rate?

options.A: Dehydration from rapid breathing thickens the circulating blood supply
options.B: The clot directly irritates the pacemaker cells inside the heart muscle
options.C: Anxiety from the hospital environment triggers an adrenaline surge
options.D: The heart pumps faster to try and push blood past the lung blockage

explanation: The heart beats faster as a way to maintain enough oxygen delivery when lung blood vessels are blocked. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T9#BMP125_U2_T9_h4)

question: A person has finished classroom lectures in a school of nursing, but has not yet passed the board exams or received a license. Can they practice independently as a nurse?

options.A: No, legal authorization by the regulatory council is required first
options.B: Yes, as long as they finished their classroom hours
options.C: Yes, under the direct verbal permission of a hospital owner
options.D: No, but they can independently prescribe simple medications

explanation: A nurse must be formally licensed and authorized by the national regulatory authority before practicing independently. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T1#BMP110_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful way to handle harmful cultural health practices?

options.A: Provide patient education explaining the health risks.
options.B: Listen patiently to understand the root cause of the practice.
options.C: Involve respected community elders to advocate for safer alternatives.
options.D: Ridicule the patient's family for being backward.

explanation: Ridicule damages trust and drives patients away from formal health facilities, whereas respectful education encourages change. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why does air naturally flow into the lungs during a normal breath?

options.A: The heart acts as a secondary pump for air movement
options.B: Active muscular contraction directly squeezes the lung tissue
options.C: A pressure difference exists between the atmosphere and alveoli
options.D: Surface tension pulls ambient air through the trachea

explanation: Air always moves down its pressure gradient, flowing from a region of higher pressure to a lower pressure area inside the chest. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T2#BMP121_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing according to Orem's foundational philosophy?

options.A: Prescribing medication for acute physical conditions
options.B: Replacing the family entirely during hospital stays
options.C: Helping individuals meet their own health needs
options.D: Taking complete control of all daily life activities

explanation: Orem viewed nursing as specialized help directed at enabling patients to regain or maintain their personal self-care abilities. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the best way for a mother to dry her perineal suture line after a gentle wash?

options.A: Rub the stitches hard with a rough towel
options.B: Pat the area gently with a clean, soft cloth
options.C: Use a hot hair dryer on the highest setting
options.D: Leave the area completely wet without touching

explanation: Patting avoids pulling or adding friction to the delicate healing tissue, whereas rubbing can break open the fresh wound edges. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h2)

question: What factor determines whether a medication acts as a sedative or a hypnotic?

options.A: The specific time of day it is swallowed
options.B: The weight and age of the pregnant woman
options.C: The administered dose of the drug
options.D: The method used to manufacture the pill

explanation: Lower doses produce a calming sedative effect, while higher doses of the same medication induce sleep as a hypnotic. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h1)

question: What does hemoglobin do when blood reaches warm, active tissues making lots of carbon dioxide?

options.A: It changes color from bright red to white
options.B: It holds onto its oxygen even tighter
options.C: It absorbs extra nitrogen gas
options.D: It releases its stored oxygen to the tissues

explanation: Active tissues generate heat and acid, signaling hemoglobin to drop off oxygen right where it is needed most. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is checking the pelvis so important in Nigerian midwifery practice?

options.A: Calculating the precise gestational age of the fetus
options.B: Determining the exact birth weight of the baby
options.C: Diagnosing early-onset pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.D: Preventing obstructed labor and maternal complications

explanation: Assessing the pelvis helps spot space limitations early, which prevents prolonged and obstructed labor that can harm the mother and baby. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T8#BMP210_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which food group gives the most stored energy gram for gram?

options.A: Fats
options.B: Vitamins
options.C: Proteins
options.D: Carbohydrates

explanation: Lipids yield more than double the calories per gram compared to carbohydrates and proteins. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the most common symptom during an ulcerative colitis flare-up?

options.A: Projectile vomiting after meals
options.B: Bloody diarrhea with mucus
options.C: Painful swallowing of food
options.D: Constipation and hard stools

explanation: Because ulcerative colitis creates sores on the inner lining of the colon, bleeding and mucus mixed with loose stool are classic signs. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T10#BMP125_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication?

options.A: Explaining how to breastfeed the baby
options.B: Asking the patient where she feels pain
options.C: Maintaining an open posture and nodding
options.D: Reading hospital admission guidelines aloud

explanation: Body language, posture, and facial expressions are forms of non-verbal communication. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T1#BMP110_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of these skeletal structures is classified as an irregular bone?

options.A: The patella
options.B: A vertebra
options.C: A rib
options.D: The humerus

explanation: Vertebrae have complex shapes designed to protect the spinal cord, making them classic examples of irregular bones. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T6#BMP111_U2_T6_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 20 weeks gestation stops taking her iron tablets because they cause mild nausea. What is the best immediate action for the midwife?

options.A: Scold her for non-compliance and document her refusal
options.B: Counsel her on taking the tablet with food or right before bed, and encourage consistent adherence
options.C: Switch her immediately to a high-dose vitamin A supplement
options.D: Tell her to stop taking all supplements permanently

explanation: Managing minor side effects practically helps keep the patient consistent with her crucial anemia-prevention routine. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T16#BMP212_U1_T16_h4)

question: Which traditional practice for swallowed poisons is dangerous and should be discouraged?

options.A: Inducing vomiting with palm oil or salt water
options.B: Bringing the empty container to the clinic
options.C: Flushing splashed eyes with clean saline
options.D: Washing the skin with soap and running water

explanation: Making a patient vomit can cause the poison to burn the throat a second time or enter the lungs, leading to severe pneumonia. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h3)

question: When is it permissible to share a patient's private health information?

options.A: When mandated by law, such as reporting specific infectious diseases or safety threats
options.B: Whenever a family member asks curiously about the patient's lab results in the hallway
options.C: Whenever the clinic waiting room is too crowded to keep records safe
options.D: When the midwife wants to discuss an interesting case with friends at home

explanation: Legal exceptions to confidentiality exist primarily to protect public health and safety, such as mandatory disease reporting or safeguarding minors. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why is internal bleeding after surgery often considered trickier to spot than external bleeding?

options.A: It does not cause any changes in blood pressure
options.B: It involves arterial blood which clots much slower
options.C: It stops spontaneously without needing any surgical intervention
options.D: It is hidden from view and harder to detect quickly

explanation: Because internal blood loss is not visible on dressings or bed sheets, a patient can lose a dangerous amount of blood before anyone notices physical symptoms. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T4#BMP120_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why are arterioles often referred to as resistance vessels?

options.A: They resist stretching when the heart pumps blood
options.B: They create the greatest opposition to blood flow due to their small size
options.C: They block the return of deoxygenated blood
options.D: They prevent white blood cells from entering tissues

explanation: The tiny size of arterioles creates substantial friction and resistance, which is the main factor controlling overall blood pressure in the body. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h5)

question: How many small bones make up the wrist in one human hand?

options.A: Twenty-seven
options.B: Fourteen
options.C: Eight
options.D: Five

explanation: There are eight small carpal bones arranged in two rows within the human wrist. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why does calculation anxiety commonly increase during emergency situations or night shifts?

options.A: Calculators stop working reliably in low lighting
options.B: Fatigue and high pressure can impair cognitive focus
options.C: Patients require higher doses of drugs after dark
options.D: Pharmacy stocks change rapidly during the night

explanation: Stressful environments and tiredness make it easier to miss small mathematical details like decimal placements. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T6#BMP120_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which muscle is the main helper for moving the thigh away from the midline and keeping the pelvis steady while walking?

options.A: Gluteus medius
options.B: Iliopsoas muscle
options.C: Gluteus maximus
options.D: Piriformis muscle

explanation: The gluteus medius and minimus work to pull the leg away from the midline and keep the pelvis level when lifting the opposite foot. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T11#BMP111_U3_T11_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical pharmacokinetic change seen during pregnancy?

options.A: Altered liver enzyme activity
options.B: Increased renal clearance
options.C: Decreased total body water volume
options.D: Elevated plasma volume

explanation: Total body water actually increases substantially during pregnancy, rather than decreasing. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which bone acts as a horizontal strut to hold the shoulder away from the body?

options.A: Sternum
options.B: Clavicle
options.C: Scapula
options.D: Humerus

explanation: The clavicle, or collarbone, keeps the arm positioned away from the chest wall. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T10#BMP111_U2_T10_h2)

question: Why must midwives consider local resource availability when choosing care actions?

options.A: To eliminate all documentation requirements in the hospital
options.B: To replace the need for physical assessments during labor
options.C: To ensure the planned actions are realistic and can be performed
options.D: To reduce the total number of patients admitted to the ward

explanation: An intervention is useless if the clinic lacks the supplies, water, or equipment required to carry it out safely. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T4#BMP120_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which health issue makes it hardest for the body to get rid of water-soluble drugs?

options.A: Renal impairment
options.B: Myocardial ischemia
options.C: Gastric hyperacidity
options.D: Pulmonary congestion

explanation: The kidneys filter out water-soluble drugs, so when kidney function is low, these medications build up in the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T6#BMP124_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which nerve supplies the muscles in the front part of the thigh?

options.A: Sciatic nerve
options.B: Tibial nerve
options.C: Femoral nerve
options.D: Obturator nerve

explanation: The femoral nerve supplies the quadriceps group in the anterior compartment, driving knee extension. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T11#BMP111_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which of the following body areas has the highest density of sebaceous glands?

options.A: The palms of the hands
options.B: The posterior lower legs
options.C: The upper face and chest
options.D: The soles of the feet

explanation: Sebaceous glands are most heavily concentrated on the face, chest, and back, which is why those areas produce the most oil. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why do midwives treat assessment as a continuous activity rather than something done just once?

options.A: Midwives have spare time during night shifts to update charts
options.B: Doctors refuse to review patients who lack hourly updates
options.C: A woman's clinical condition and needs can change rapidly during labor
options.D: Hospital regulations require rewriting admission notes every shift

explanation: Maternity conditions are dynamic, meaning a stable mother can develop complications quickly, requiring continuous reassessment. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the genetic cause behind sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: A complete absence of alpha-globin genes on chromosome 16
options.B: A single amino acid substitution in the beta-globin chain
options.C: A premature destruction of platelets by splenic macrophages
options.D: An excess of dietary iron accumulation in liver tissues

explanation: Sickle cell anaemia happens due to a tiny change in one amino acid within the beta-globin chain. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T5#BMP111_U5_T5_h6)

question: Around how many weeks of pregnancy are Leopold's maneuvers usually reliable for feeling the baby's position?

options.A: 24 weeks
options.B: 12 weeks
options.C: 16 weeks
options.D: 20 weeks

explanation: Before 24 weeks, the baby is too small compared to the amount of water around it, making it hard to feel positions clearly. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why must a nurse check a colleague's training level before handing over a task?

options.A: To make sure every shift lasts the exact same duration
options.B: To reduce the salary budget allocated for the ward
options.C: To ensure patient safety and legal accountability
options.D: To ensure all senior staff avoid doing physical work

explanation: Delegating tasks beyond a worker's training level puts patients at risk and breaches professional nursing regulations. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h4)

question: How do the levator ani muscles help direct the mechanism of labor as the baby descends?

options.A: They contract forcefully to push the baby out without maternal effort
options.B: They seal the cervix shut until crowning occurs
options.C: They absorb all amniotic fluid to keep the birth canal dry
options.D: Their slope helps guide the fetal head to rotate forward

explanation: The downward and forward slope of the resting pelvic floor acts like a slide, helping the presenting part rotate correctly toward the front of the pelvis. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T7#BMP210_U1_T7_h5)

question: A student midwife examining a pelvic bone notices a very narrow, heart-shaped pelvic inlet and a sharp pubic angle. What is the likely sex of this pelvis?

options.A: Infant
options.B: Female
options.C: Child
options.D: Male

explanation: A narrow, heart-shaped inlet and acute pubic angle are classic skeletal traits of the male pelvis. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T12#BMP111_U2_T12_h4)

question: A midwife gently moves a relaxed client's knee through its motion limits while the client rests. What is this called?

options.A: Passive range of motion
options.B: Manual muscle grading
options.C: Reflex hammer testing
options.D: Active range of motion

explanation: When the examiner moves the relaxed client's joint, it is a passive range of motion assessment. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the skeletal system?

options.A: Releasing hormones that influence blood sugar levels
options.B: Storing chemical energy within yellow bone marrow
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes to break down proteins
options.D: Buffering blood pH by absorbing or releasing salts

explanation: Digestive enzymes are produced by organs like the stomach, pancreas, and small intestine, not by the skeletal system. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T1#BMP111_U2_T1_h5)

question: How does too much noise in a hospital ward affect a patient?

options.A: It disrupts sleep and can raise blood pressure
options.B: It increases germs on ward surfaces
options.C: It causes immediate breathing difficulties
options.D: It speeds up the breakdown of intravenous drugs

explanation: High noise levels cause physical stress, interfering with the rest required for tissue repair and healing. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T9#BMP110_U5_T9_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT checked during a routine wound assessment?

options.A: The depth and size of the wound
options.B: The amount and type of wound drainage
options.C: The patient's shoe size
options.D: The condition of the surrounding skin

explanation: Shoe size has no relevance to wound assessment, whereas drainage, surrounding skin health, and wound dimensions are vital clinical indicators. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which protein makes up thick myofilaments?

options.A: Actin
options.B: Myosin
options.C: Troponin
options.D: Tropomyosin

explanation: Thick filaments are built from bundled molecules of the protein myosin. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h3)

question: What does a single umbilical artery mean for the structure of the cord?

options.A: All three normal vessels have fused into a single tube
options.B: The cord contains two veins and no arteries at all
options.C: The umbilical vein has split into two separate channels
options.D: Only one artery is present alongside one vein

explanation: A single umbilical artery means the cord has a total of two vessels instead of the normal three. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h3)

question: Which item is best to keep ready at the bedside when preparing an admission bed?

options.A: Admission chart and a clean hospital gown
options.B: A heavy surgical instrument tray and suture materials
options.C: A pair of sterile obstetrical forceps and a fetal scope
options.D: An empty kidney basin filled with concentrated bleach

explanation: Having the chart and gown ready immediately streamlines the admission process and welcomes the client with dignity. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which type of shock is directly caused by a massive loss of blood after surgery?

options.A: Hypovolemic shock
options.B: Septic shock
options.C: Cardiogenic shock
options.D: Anaphylactic shock

explanation: Hypovolemic shock happens when the volume of blood or fluid in the body drops too low to maintain pressure. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T5#BMP120_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical sign of a broken bone?

options.A: Severe localized pain
options.B: Instant muscle paralysis
options.C: Rapid swelling
options.D: Visible limb deformity
